explanation: Author of the book of Ecclesiastes, believed to be King Solomon, who shares his wisdom and reflections on the meaning of life.
A central theme in the book of Ecclesiastes, used to describe the futility and transience of human endeavors and worldly pleasures.
Another important theme in the book, emphasizing that there is a time for everything under heaven and that God has appointed a time for every purpose.
The ability to understand and apply knowledge in a way that leads to good choices and actions. The Preacher values wisdom but also recognizes its limitations.
Human effort and activity aimed at achieving a goal. The Preacher reflects on the meaning of work and its outcomes, both positive and negative.
Enjoyment and joy that people seek in life. The Preacher explores the value of pleasure and its place in the search for life's meaning.
Respect and awe toward God, regarded as the foundation of a meaningful life and wisdom. The Preacher recommends fearing God and keeping His commandments.
God's just evaluation and assessment of human actions. The Preacher reminds us that God will judge everything, both good and evil.
